name: Jelski's Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: East slope of andes from southeastern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe) southward to central peru (to junín)
description: Rare flycatcher found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru, barely reaching over the border into southeastern Ecuador. Male is dark sooty gray; female is grayish-olive with pale wingbars and faint streaking below.

name: Caspian Tern
rangeDescription: Breeds patchily coastal baltic sea and inland southeast europe to western mongolia and ussuriland (southeastern russia) and northeastern china and southern asian coasts; coastal and inland western and southern africa; europa (west of southern madagascar, mozambique channel), coastal madagascar and aldabra group (southwestern seychelles); coastal and inland northern and eastern australia, coastal new zealand (north, south and stewart islands); inland northwest territories to northeastern canada, in south to central california and great lakes; winters to coastal africa, red sea, persian gulf, india, thailand, malay peninsula, and vietnam; eastern pacific and caribbean to panama
description: Largest tern in the world; widespread but typically uncommon. Thick, bright-red bill is distinctive; most have small dark marking near the tip.

name: Wreathed Hornbill
rangeDescription: Northeastern india to southwestern china, southeastern asia, and greater sundas
description: A large and stately hornbill of expansive montane forests. Both sexes are black with snow-white tails.

name: Trinidad Piping-Guan
rangeDescription: Forest of trinidad (endangered)
description: Large, turkey-like bird found only in the forests of northern Trinidad. It is black with white patches on the wings and crown, a light blue face, and an azure dewlap (flap of bare skin) that dangles from its throat.

name: Erckel's Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Northeastern sudan and highlands of northern eritrea and northwestern ethiopia; introduced to hawaii
description: A pheasant-sized game bird with a chestnut crown, white throat, and white streaks above and below. Males are larger than females.

name: Slaty-backed Thornbill
rangeDescription: Mulga areas of central western australia to south-central queensland
description: Small bird with thin pointed bill, uncommon in mulga woodland of arid inland temperate Australia. Brownish gray above, cream-colored below, with dark eye, dark streaking on forecrown, pale lores, pale-tipped dark tail, and chestnut rump, often visible in flight.

name: Hispaniolan Nightjar
rangeDescription: Hispaniola
description: Dark brown and buff nocturnal bird often first noted by its distinctive song, a low, burry “pit, whoo-vore?”, often given in rapid succession. Similar to migratory Chuck-will’s-widow, but plumage is darker and less buffy, and tail is tipped white in male or buff in female, though this may only be evident when seen from below.

name: White-faced Ground-Sparrow
rangeDescription: Highlands of southern mexico (chiapas) guatemala, el salvador, and western honduras
description: Rather local large sparrow of foothills and highlands in Chiapas and northern Central America. Found in brushy woodland and edge and overgrown clearings; usually on or near the ground and often in pairs.

name: White-crowned Pigeon
rangeDescription: Southern florida and offshore islands from west indies to northwestern panama
description: Large dark pigeon, entirely dark gray with contrasting white cap. Pink legs and pink bill with a pale tip.

name: Tsingy Forest Rail
rangeDescription: Local in west-central madagascar (bemaraha and beanka massifs)
description: Chunky rail-like bird with rich rufous coloration. Found on the floor of dry forest in and adjacent to the limestone karst “tsingy” of Bemaraha and Beanka.

name: Marañon Crescentchest
rangeDescription: Far southern ecuador (southern zamora-chinchipe) and adjacent northern peru
description: Gorgeous little bird with a small range in the Marañon Valley of northwestern Peru and adjacent border areas of Ecuador (south of Zumba). Note the black mask, white eyebrow and throat, rich chestnut underparts, and white edges to wing feathers.

name: Buffy Helmetcrest
rangeDescription: Central andes of colombia (quindío and tolima)
description: Large, short-billed hummingbird found only at extremely high elevations in Colombia’s central Andes. Adult male’s green and blue beard, black and buff head pattern, and shaggy crest make him easily recognizable within his tiny world range.

name: Nilgiri Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Western ghats and coastal southwestern india
description: Small plain gray-brown bird with a slightly curved bill. Nearly identical to Plain Flowerpecker, but ranges do not overlap.

name: Black-faced Munia
rangeDescription: Lowlands of wallacea (except for lesser sundas)
description: A striking finch with a black hood, light brown collar, extensively barred white underside, and pale barred rump. Juveniles duller, brown above and buffy below, lacking bars.

name: Gray-headed Piprites
rangeDescription: Caribbean lowlands of eastern guatemala to costa rica
description: Confusing forest species, rare and difficult to find among mixed flocks. Typically stays at middle levels.

name: Andaman Treepie
rangeDescription: Dense forest of andaman islands
description: A slender, medium-sized dark bird with a long tail. The face, wings, and tail are black, while the underparts and back are reddish-brown.

name: Magenta-throated Woodstar
rangeDescription: Highlands of northern costa rica and western panama
description: Tiny hummingbird with long tail often cocked up. Slow bumblebee-like flight.

name: Scrub Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Foothills of southern new guinea
description: A medium-sized honeyeater of foothill and mid-mountain scrub. Uniform olive green with a white ear spot and indistinct streak in the base of the bill.

name: Tongan Megapode
rangeDescription: Forest of niuafo'ou (northwestern tonga); recently introduced to late and fonualei, and populations formerly on other tongan islands have died out
description: A plump, mostly ground-dwelling bird with long yellowish legs and a dark gray body with slightly browner wash on the wings and back. Head mostly dark gray, with bright orange beak and whitish crest.

name: Swainson's Hawk
rangeDescription: Western north america; winters to northern argentina, southern brazil, and paraguay
description: Longer-winged than Red-tailed Hawk, but otherwise the same size. Found in prairies and agricultural regions of western U.S.
